book_title: When I Think of My Body as a Horse
subject_line: Spelt, the Yorkshire coast and When I Think of My Body as a Horse
email_body:
Dear Wendy,

I came across When I Think of My Body as a Horse through its Poetry Business Book and Pamphlet award, and then found that you also founded and edit Spelt Magazine while living and working on the North Yorkshire coast. I would be curious to hear how editing other people's writing about rural life sits alongside writing your own poems, and whether the coast shapes both in the same way.

book_title: All The Men I Never Married
subject_line: Kendal Poetry Festival and All The Men I Never Married
email_body:
Dear Kim,

I noticed that alongside writing All The Men I Never Married and teaching creative writing at Manchester Metropolitan University, you co-direct Kendal Poetry Festival and host a monthly reading series for Wordsworth Grasmere. That is a lot of time spent listening to other poets in Cumbria. I would like to ask how running readings and a festival has changed the way you hear your own work, and what the region gives you that a bigger city might not.

subject_line: From the NorthBound Award to Kingfisher on the shelf
email_body:
Dear Rozie,

I read that Kingfisher won New Writing North's NorthBound Book Award in 2023 and came out with Saraband in 2025, and that you have since talked at the University of York about publishing a debut novel. That path from award manuscript to finished book is something readers rarely see. I would like to ask what changed in Kingfisher between the award and publication, and what you wish you had known at the start.
